You seek to become more than what you are. In the heat of battle or in life’s most tranquil moments, you reach for a greater state to reach transcendence, self-improvement, or a hint of divinity. You’ve devoted yourself to a philosophy that imparts lessons and ideals for spiritual fulfillment. You utter meditations that lifts your spirit high, entering a trance that taps into a great power that exemplifies the ideals you are dedicated to. During moments of zeniths, your heightened self brings the divine to the world.

Key Ability: DEXTERITY

At 1st level, your class gives you an attribute boost to Dexterity.

Hit Points: 8 plus your Constitution modifier

You increase your maximum number of HP by this number at 1st level and every level thereafter.

Roleplaying the Dervish

During Combat Encounters...

You enter a combat trance, reciting meditations mentally or verbally as you move and act in ways appropriate to your chosen parable. In the moment during your trance, you feel closer to the concepts you envision, reaching a spiritual high that lets you unleash divine powers.

During Social Encounters...

You try to act according to the philosophies you embody. You might reject certain acts or try to behave in certain ways to live up to chosen standards, and become more than you are in your daily life.

While Exploring...

You recount your parables and take heed of its lessons, to be aware of things you should do or avoid in your surroundings. You try to apply your learnings to situations you encounter on the road.

In Downtime...

You spend your time improving yourself and practicing the lessons of your parables in a safer context. You might go into study or confer with philosophers about the world or the divine, or learn new meditations and understand how it can be embedded into your philosophies.

You Might...

●       Try and find a lesson that might apply in any scenario before you.

●       Strive for loftier goals and try to reach new spiritual heights.

●       Study new ideas and lessons both practical and philosophical.

Others Probably…

●       View you as a religious scholar, whether it may be true or not.

●       Look to you for timely and sage advice.

●       Be perplexed when you enter your meditative trances.

You are a bastion of talent and creativity. While you can grasp magic, you see possibilities that extend beyond simple rote applications or manifestations bestowed by other entities. Some might think you a spellcaster bestowed with innate talent, but that isn’t your gift – no, you don’t cast magic, you create magic. You are a creator that wields the tools of expression, envisioning what magic could be. Some might call you apocryphal, or even mistake you for a fake, talentless trickster. But you are an erudite and a visionary both; with a little bit of planning and a sprinkle of catalyzing reagents, you can express magic in beautiful, colorful ways.

Key Ability: INTELLIGENCE OR CHARISMA

At 1st level, your class gives you an attribute boost to Intelligence or Charisma, depending on your artifex’s medium.

Hit Points: 6 plus your Constitution modifier

You increase your maximum number of HP by this number at 1st level and every level thereafter.

Roleplaying the Artifex

During Combat Encounters...

You sprinkle your magical catalysts to manifest your spells in unconventional ways and exploit the fabric of magic to create fantastical effects that explode in myriad colors, lights, or patterns.

During Social Encounters...

You bring forth creative ideas to the table, using unique insights from your keen intellect tempered by your desire to see things not as they are, but what they could be.

While Exploring...

You find novel and intriguing ways to apply magic to uniquely solve your roadblocks and look for unique ingredients you can pick up and turn into catalysts.

In Downtime...

You look for inspirations and ideas to create brand new ways to interpret magic, and debate and draft your ideas to peers who could listen in social or academic settings. You might also spend time to create novel shows and displays of your magic to entertain or to educate.

You Might...

  • Keep a record that lists your favorite catalysts, and the best times to use which exploits.

  • Spend time drawing or drafting ideas for your next great display of magical genius.

  • Go out of your way to one-up people who wield magic in their conventional ways.

Others Probably…

  • Think of you as an eccentric sorcerer.

  • Be captivated or impressed at the explosive output of your magic.

  • Consider you as a trickster who uses tools to fool others into thinking you are a spellcaster.

Through profane alchemical experiments, your body contains two souls bound together: yours, and that of a monster. Your soul wrestles for constant control with your pair, and a hunger gnaws at you both to devour other souls or risk cannibalizing one another. For this terrible price, however, you have gained the power to draw upon your anima maelstrom, allowing you to manifest the abilities of even the most dangerous creatures of the world.

Key Ability: Wisdom or other

At 1st level, your class gives you an attribute boost to Wisdom, or another attribute depending on your anima manifestation.

Hit Points: 8 plus your Constitution modifier

You increase your maximum number of HP by this number at 1st level and every level thereafter.

Roleplaying the Chimerian

During Combat Encounters...

You invoke your anima to unleash powerful magic upon your enemies or to support your companions, as the situation demands. With every victory, your prey joins the maelstrom of consumed souls and adds to your power.

During Social Encounters...

You often speak with pragmatic and often blunt insights as social scenarios are often off-putting, but your paired soul might be one that finds these situations fascinating and curious.

While Exploring...

You rely on the various gifts and powers of the right soul in your maelstrom to keep an eye out for threats. If you are someplace new, you would be on alert looking for a suitably powerful creature whose powers might help you traverse unfamiliar terrain.

In Downtime...

You might spend your time appeasing or domineering your paired soul, keeping its instincts in check or reaching a state of calm. Through key moments reflecting on your relationship with your bonded soul, you grow more confident and capable as a pair.

You Might...

●       Struggle to keep your paired soul in check; the bonded soul fights for control of your body, and if its needs aren't met, you are forced to wrestle with its instincts.

●       Look for stronger creatures that could sate your hunger and grow your maelstrom of souls.

●       Meditate upon the relationship between you and your bonded soul.

Others Probably…

●       View you as a wild hybrid of man and monster, especially if your body shows any signs of monstrous mutations.

●       Fear that you might hunt them for their souls.

●       Sympathize or empathize with your inner conflict.

Chimerian Ethics

Due to its design, the chimerian is a class that may not be a fit for parties or campaigns that views souls of the dead as sacred. The act of consuming the soul as described in the Anima Maelstrom feature is meant to evoke uncomfortable questions of the nature of the chimerian’s power.

In some instances, a Chimerian may not have had a choice in becoming one; they are constantly at odds with a second soul that belongs to a monster, and they both share a gnawing hunger for anima – and souls are a rife source for it. They know that the body requires the anima to maintain coherency and survival. It is a character trope that is sometimes seen in media, questioning the ethics of survival in man blurring into a monster, such as vampires or werewolves.

The nature of the class may not be suitable for some parties or campaigns, so if a player wants to pursue the class but the table would prefer to avoid these themes, a GM could eschew the permanent consumption of the soul of the dead and treat the anima power as learning the power of those departed and then releasing it after the fact. This act could also sate the twin souls’ need to drain anima for sustaining the maelstrom and maintaining souls’ cohesion. A GM may also exclude certain traits such as Humanoid from the list of creatures available for Soulreave.

Chimerian Anima Magic

@Embed[Compendium.immortal-ardor.classes.Item.A7tdCuCuYTjcAB1P inline hr=false]

Learning New Spells as a Chimerian

Learning new spells as a Chimerian requires that the chimerian takes the soul of a creature into their own, or in a possible variant of play learn the power from a creature after they have passed. As a result, the narrative and the campaign structure plays a heavy role in determining what a player might be able to get – after all, if they never encounter a creature that has a spell they want, they might never get it!

There is a mode of campaign that lets a chimerian player roll with what the GM provides them; this is very similar to how spellcasters with a repository of learned spells, like Wizards and Witches must be able to scribe spells into their repository – though they gain spells automatically into their repository as they level up, and also have means during Downtime to acquire new spells, such as scribing from scrolls, other spellbooks, or learning from other practitioners in town. In this instance, it is important that the GM provides the chimerian player opportunities to encounter or hunt for creatures that might grant them the spells they are interested in throughout their adventure.

However, in some instances the campaign might never truly afford them that opportunity that makes sense for narrative flow – if a campaign is about the war between celestials and fiends, it might be hard to fit in narratively prominent encounters with creatures from the astral or fey planes without breaking the story’s flow. In this case, the GM might consider having the chimerian Gather Information or Track certain creature families during downtime to provide them with an off-screen chance to find and acquire the spell they are seeking without breaking narrative pacing, or even finding a morally ambiguous or repugnant peddler of souls, seeking to sell to a hungry chimerian. An even simpler alternative would be to allowing a chimerian player to gain one spell automatically as they gain in levels, handwaving how they acquired it as a distant evolution from a soul they have consumed.

At 2nd level and every 2 levels thereafter, you gain a skill feat. You must be trained or better in the corresponding skill to select a skill feat.

General FeatsLevel 3

At 3rd level and every 4 levels thereafter, you gain a general feat.

Skill IncreasesLevel 3

At 3rd level and every 2 levels thereafter, you gain a skill increase. You can use this increase to either become trained in one skill you’re untrained in, or become an expert in one skill in which you’re already trained.

At 7th level, you can use skill increases to become a master in a skill in which you’re already an expert, and at 15th level, you can use them to become legendary in a skill in which you’re already a master.
